links.outcome: Share of agents changing triage decision across equivalent consensus prompt wordings (urgent vs neutral vs none)
links.effect: 56.7% of agents changed decision under the original urgent wording vs 15.8% and 7.2% under the neutral and no-consensus wordings; a single agent changed 43.4% vs 12.6%.
links.quote: Under the original wording 56.7 per cent of agents stated a different decision in the last round than in the first, against 15.8 and 7.2 per cent under the other wordings.

links.outcome: Sensitivity of LLM triage decisions to prompt wording variation
links.effect: Decision changes followed the consensus wording: 56.7% under urgent wording vs 15.8% and 7.2% under other wordings, also seen in single agents (43.4% vs 12.6%).
links.quote: We find that the shifts follow the consensus wording and occur without peers' answers, though a contribution of peers is not excluded; deployed systems were not studied.
